languages.notes: Практический полевой профиль: перечислены языки, с которыми путешественник реально столкнётся в регионе; это не полный этнолингвистический перечень.

climate.summary: Coastal/western Sarawak receives a strong northeast-monsoon signal: December–March are especially wet and January is typically the maximum; coastal minimum tends to occur around June–July.

floods.risk_context: DID operates multiple Kuching river-level stations in the Sungai Sarawak system; use live levels during prolonged rain.

climate.best_period_general: Более сухие месяцы, но дождь возможен всегда.

geography.summary: Широкий западно-северный коридор Sarawak; в текущем legacy-region объединены Kuching/Sarawak Delta и удалённый Niah возле Miri, поэтому факты, относящиеся только к одной части, помечаются явно.
geography.delta: Sarawak Delta UNESCO Global Geopark around Kuching includes an extensive river-delta system and transition from low plains to higher inland ground.

geology.sarawak_delta: UNESCO describes the Kuching Zone suture as evidence of collision between ancient landmasses more than 200 million years ago; the geopark preserves a geological record exceeding 250 million years.
geology.niah: Niah is a limestone cave/karst and archaeological landscape, but detailed cave geology remains attached to the Niah object until a dedicated Niah locality profile is formalized.

nature.niah: Sarawak Forestry describes Niah as lowland rainforest with bats, swiftlets, endemic Niah Cave gecko, birds, butterflies, squirrels, monkeys and occasional hornbills.

health.interpretation: State-level historical reference for 2022; Kuching and Niah cannot be assigned the same current risk.

transport.niah: Sarawak Forestry places park HQ roughly two hours by road from Miri or Bintulu; access continues by motorised boat across Niah River and about one hour on raised plankwalk to Great Cave.
